name: DARWIN
full_name: DARk matter WImp search with liquid xenoN
summary: DARWIN is the historical large liquid-xenon observatory design for dark matter, solar and supernova neutrinos, and xenon-136 double-beta decay. Its collaboration helped form the larger XLZD programme; the two concepts must not be counted as two completed facilities.
detection_principle: A dual-phase xenon time projection chamber records prompt scintillation and delayed electroluminescence. Low backgrounds and a large isotope inventory enable electron-recoil, nuclear-recoil and rare-decay searches.

results.summary: Published DARWIN studies present neutrino and double-beta sensitivity forecasts. The subsequent DARWIN/XLZD development does not constitute an observed neutrinoless-decay signal.

science_scope: A neutrinoless decay would violate lepton number. Half-life sensitivity is a forecast unless explicitly reported as an experimental limit; its interpretation as an effective Majorana mass depends on the decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements.
